performance_tasks.brief: Cycle 1, water access and survey design: original supplied-investigation pack, 35 marks in total. Compose subparts using only observed primary-command/tariff pairs; each part is at most six marks. Plan the enquiry, apply sampling/data collection, pilot an instrument, organise and interpret supplied original data, and solve a practical research obstacle. Supply all context and datasets. AO B10/C18/D7 is a planner split, not an official Section A grid. Use distinct tasks and original figures in each cycle.
performance_tasks.objective_ids: choose 2-4 objectives from this topic that the task genuinely exercises

performance_tasks.brief: Cycle 1, water access and survey design: own-investigation rehearsal, 15 marks in subparts of at most six. Model the reasoning first with a clearly fictional completed enquiry and its data, then supply prompts to transfer the method to the learner’s actual investigation. Link research question, aims, methods, findings, evidence, conclusion, recommendation, implementer and limitations. Never invent a learner’s actual fieldwork. Keep the personal report requirement. AO B5/C7/D3 is a planner split. This paired cycle totals the syllabus Paper 3 split B15/C25/D10.

ao_mix_note: The syllabus states its AO weights as a share of MARKS, so planned_ao_mix_by_marks is the one that answers "does this resource match the exam". It values each card at the tariff of the question it models, split across the AOs the card declares, and values each performance task at the marks of the paper part it models. The count-based mix below is reported only because it is what a reader expects to see; do not balance against it. AO shares by ITEM COUNT: Every objective needs one recall anchor, so AO1 has a structural floor of about 52% in this topic (36 objectives against 69 slots) and cannot reach the None% target by count however many other cards are added - padding the bank to chase it makes the resource worse. The framework already measures the AO4 share in practice time rather than by count for the same reason. Treat AO1 above target as expected, and AO2/AO3/AO4 below target as the thing worth fixing.
